notes: Manual behavioral evals. In a fresh session, compare the same prompt with and without this skill using the same model and tools. Grade the response against assertions only after generation; these cases are not run by a repository test runner.

evals.name: introduced-regression
evals.prompt: Review this diff against the prior behavior. A TypeScript helper changed from `return items.filter(Boolean)` to `return items.filter(x => x.id)`; callers pass records where `id` can be 0, and the API treats 0 as a valid identifier. The existing test suite does not cover id 0. Report actionable findings.
assertions: Identifies that valid id 0 records are dropped and ties it to the changed line.
States a realistic trigger and user-visible consequence with an appropriate severity.
Does not edit code or report unrelated style preferences.

evals.name: unclear-comparison-scope
evals.prompt: Review the repository for the regression. I did not provide a base revision, branch, PR, or file list, and the working tree contains changes in several unrelated areas.
assertions: Asks which comparison point or changed scope to review before analyzing unrelated changes.
Does not present speculative findings as confirmed.

evals.name: clean-change
evals.prompt: Review this diff. It adds `limitItems(items, limit)` in `src/limit.ts`. When `limit` is omitted, it returns the original full list; when supplied, it requires a nonnegative integer and returns `items.slice(0, limit)`. The diff also adds tests for omitted, zero, positive, negative, and fractional limits. Existing callers do not pass the new argument. Report only actionable issues.
assertions: Reports no actionable issues if none are evidenced.
Summarizes the reviewed scope and any meaningful validation limit.
Does not invent a finding to fill the report.
